rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، السدي، ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: “Their plotting” means their talk criticizing the wife of al-Aziz after she disclosed her affair and they exposed the secret.
rows.anchor: قولهن وعيبهن لها قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He explains calling their speech “plotting”: they knew her secret, then schemed by publicizing it.
rows.anchor: لأنها كانت أطلعتهن على أمرها واستكتمتهن فمكرن وأفشين سرها

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The women really plotted against her, speaking that way in order to make her show them Joseph.
rows.anchor: أنه مكر حقيقة وإنما قلن ذلك مكرا بها لتريهن يوسف قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: “Prepared” derives from equipment or provision; an item made ready for a purpose is a lasting requisite.
rows.anchor: أفعلت من العتاد وكل ما اتخذته عدة لشيء فهو عتاد

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He glosses “prepared” as “made ready.”
rows.anchor: أعتدت بمعنى أعدت

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The “reclining place” was a gathering place that she prepared for the women.
rows.anchor: أنه المجلس فالمعنى هيأت لهن مجلسا قاله الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The “reclining place” means cushions on which the women leaned.
rows.anchor: أنه الوسائد اللائي يتكئن عليها قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: A reclining place is what people lean on while eating, drinking, or conversing.
rows.anchor: المتكأ ما يتكأ عليه لطعام أو شراب أو حديث

rows.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: They interpret the reclining place as food; the idiom “we reclined at so-and-so’s” means we ate there.
rows.anchor: أنه الطعام قاله الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة قال ابن قتيبة يقال اتكأنا عند فلان إذا طعمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By metonymy, food is called a reclining place because a guest invited to eat is given a seat and comfort for staying.
rows.anchor: فسمي الطعام متكأ على الاستعارة

rows.speaker: جميل بن معمر
rows.claim: His verse uses “reclined” for dining and drinking, supporting the food interpretation.
rows.anchor: فظللنا في نعمة واتكأنا وشربنا الحلال من قلله

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Food was called a reclining place because diners sit and lean; this community was forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: لأن القوم إذا قعدوا على الطعام اتكؤوا ونهيت هذه الأمة عن ذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He read mutka with a light, still tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد متكا باسكان التاء خفيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: On the light reading, mutka means citron.
rows.anchor: أنه الأترج قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد ويحيى بن يعمر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses mutk for citron, supporting that interpretation of the light reading.
rows.anchor: وترى المتك بيننا مستعارا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He also explains mutka as food.
rows.anchor: أنه الطعام أيضا قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He interprets mutka as anything cut with knives.
rows.anchor: أنه كل شيء يحز بالسكاكين قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another report from him identifies mutka as a dish of vegetables and meat (zammāward).
rows.anchor: أنه الزماورد روي عن الضحاك أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He says the mutka was citron and, more generally, anything cut with knives.
rows.anchor: المتكأ الأترج وكل ما يحز بالسكاكين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He distinguishes the readings: the heavy reading means food, while the light reading means citron.
rows.anchor: من قرأ متكأ بالتثقيل فهو الطعام ومن قرأ بالتخفيف فهو الأترج

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He associates the light reading with citron or zammāward.
rows.anchor: من قرأ متكا فإنه يريد الأترج ويقال الزماورد

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He derives mutka from cutting: it may come from batk with bāʾ replaced by mīm, a substitution found in Arabic.
rows.anchor: إلا بالقطع كأنه مأخوذ من البتك فأبدلت الميم منه باء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women were given knives because the food served required them.
rows.anchor: إنما فعلت ذلك لأن الطعام الذي قدمت لهن يحتاج إلى السكاكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that she intended to expose them through cutting their hands, just as they had exposed her.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان مقصودها افتضاحهن بتقطيع أيديهن كما فضحنها

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: She handed each woman a citron and knife, telling them not to cut or eat until she instructed them.
rows.anchor: ناولَت كل واحدة منهن أترجة وسكينا وقالت لهن لا تقطعن ولا تأكلن حتى أعلمكن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: In “she said,” either fatḥa or ḍamma on the tāʾ is read; kasra is the default, while ḍamma follows the preceding kasra.
rows.anchor: إن شئت ضممت التاء من قوله وقالت وإن شئت كسرت والكسر الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She could not refuse the order to come out because she was effectively his owner.
rows.anchor: ولم يمكنه أن لا يخرج لأنه بمنزلة العبد لها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: She said “come out” while inwardly supplying “to them”; revelation reports the intended inner speech as if spoken.
rows.anchor: أضمرت في نفسها عليهن فأخبر الحق عما في النفس كأن اللسان قد نطق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports that explanation by noting she would not tell a handsome young man to appear before tempting women.
rows.anchor: أنها لو قالت له وهو شاب مستحسن اخرج على نسوة من طبعهن الفتنة ما فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾanic phrase “We feed you for God’s sake” likewise expresses an inward intention; the people did not say it aloud.
rows.anchor: ومثله ( إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله ) الآية

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد، قتادة، ابن زيد
rows.claim: “They were overwhelmed by him” means they considered him magnificent and were awed by him.
rows.anchor: أعظمنه رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد وبه قال قتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: “They were overwhelmed by him” means they menstruated.
rows.anchor: حضن رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي بن عبد الله عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reports that they menstruated from joy.
rows.anchor: حضن من الفرح قال

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: His verse uses “when women menstruate” as evidence for the unusual sense of akbarna.
rows.anchor: ولا نأتي النساء إذا أكبرن إكبارا

rows.speaker: ليث عن مجاهد
rows.claim: He also transmits the menstruation interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقد روى هذا المعنى ليث عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He chooses the menstruation interpretation of akbarna.
rows.anchor: واختاره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He rejects “menstruated” as a normal Arabic meaning, allowing only that intense astonishment might have caused menstruation.
rows.anchor: ليس في كلام العرب أكبرن بمعنى حضن ولكن عسى أن يكن من شدة ما أعظمنه حضن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He also rejects interpreting akbarna as menstruation.
rows.anchor: وكذلك روي عن الزجاج أنه أنكره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن زيد
rows.claim: One interpretation of cutting their hands is that they nicked them, thinking they were cutting food.
rows.anchor: أحدها حززن أيديهن وكن يحسبن أنهن يقطعن طعاما قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: They cut their hands so deeply that the hands fell off.
rows.anchor: قطعن أيديهن حتى ألقينها قاله مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: They wounded their palms and fingertips.
rows.anchor: كلمن الأكف وابن الأنامل قاله وهب بن منبه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: He reads ḥāshā with a final alif in connected recitation at both occurrences; all omit it in pause.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو حاشا بألف في الوصل في الموضعين واتفقوا عن حذف الألف في الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāshā is used both for exception and for declaring someone free of evil; its root denotes being at someone's side or in a region.
rows.anchor: هذه الكلمة تستعمل في موضعين أحدهما الاستثناء والثاني التبرئة من الشر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses ḥashā to mean a region or direction.
rows.anchor: بأي الحشا أمسى الخليط المباين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: They gloss ḥāshā li-llāh as “God forbid.”
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد حاش لله بمعنى معاذ الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Because Hijaz speakers normally use the preposition bāʾ with bashar, dropping it leaves the predicate accusative as a trace of the omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء و بشرا منصوب لأن الباء قد استعملت فيه فلا يكاد اهل الحجاز ينطقون إلا بالباء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Najdi speakers use the bāʾ or omit it; with omission they use nominative, which he calls the stronger Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل نجد فيتكلمون بالباء وبغير الباء فإذا أسقطوها رفعوا وهو أقوى الوجهين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that nominative is linguistically stronger: the language of God's Book is strongest, and no one recited the nominative.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج قوله الرفع أقوى الوجيهن غلط لأن كتاب الله أقوى اللغات ولم يقرأ بالرفع أحد

rows.speaker: الخليل، سيبويه، النحويون القدماء
rows.claim: They analyze basharan as the accusative predicate of mā, which functions like laysa.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل وسيبويه وجميع النحويين القدماء أن بشرا منصوب لأنه خبر ما و ما بمنزلة ليس

rows.speaker: أبو المتوكل، أبو نهيك، عكرمة، معاذ القارئ
rows.claim: They recited “this is not a human” with bashar in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو المتوكل وابو نهيك و عكرمة ومعاذ القارئ في آخرين ما هذا بشر بالرفع

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب، أبو الجوزاء، أبو السوار
rows.claim: They recited basharā with kasra on bāʾ and shīn, as a shortened, nunated word.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وأبو الجوزاء وأبو السوار ما هذا بشرى بكسر الباء والشين مقصورا منونا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He recited bishirāʾ, lengthened and hamzated in the genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود بشراء بالمد والهمز مخفوضا منونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same omission of bāʾ is compared with the construction in al-Mujādilah 58:2.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله ( ماهن أمهاتهم )

rows.speaker: أبي، أبو رزين، عكرمة، أبو حيوة، الجحدري
rows.claim: They recited malak with kasra on the lām.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبي وأبو رزين وعكرمة وأبو حيوة والجحدري ملك بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Joseph promised to tell the prisoners about food before it reached them in waking life, as knowledge of the unseen like Jesus’ knowledge.
rows.anchor: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه في اليقظة إلا أخبرتكما به قبل أن يصل إليكما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Joseph meant that he would interpret food seen in a dream before it arrived in waking life.
rows.anchor: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه في المنام إلا نبأتكما بتأويله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The prisoners asked how Joseph could know this when he was neither a magician, soothsayer, nor astrologer; he answered that his Lord taught him.
rows.anchor: فقالا له وكيف تعلم ذلك ولست بساحر ولا عراف ولا صاحب نجوم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Joseph turned from the requested dream interpretation because he knew one prisoner would be killed and called them to their share in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لما علم أن أحدهما مقتول دعاهما إلى نصيبهما من الآخرة قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Joseph avoided interpreting the dream because its outcome would be painful for one prisoner.
rows.anchor: عدل عن الجواب لما فيه من المكروه لأحدهما قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Joseph began by inviting them to faith before answering their question.
rows.anchor: أنه ابتدأ بدعائهما إلى الإيمان قبل جواب السؤال قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Joseph thought the prisoners' dreams were fabricated and avoided answering until their insistence made him respond.
rows.anchor: ظنهما كاذبين في رؤياهما فعدل عن جوابهما ليعرضا عن مطالبته بالجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milla means religion, and repeating “they” adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: فأما الملة فهي الدين وتكرير قوله ( هم ) للتوكيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God protected the forefathers from associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: يريد أن الله عصمنا من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following faith was God's favor through His enabling guidance.
rows.anchor: اتباعنا الإيمان بتوفيق الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The favor to Joseph's family was making them prophets; toward people it was sending them as messengers.
rows.anchor: ذلك من فضل الله عينا أن جعلنا أنبياء ( وعلى الناس ) أن بعثنا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people in Egypt fail to thank God by affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: أكثر الناس من أهل مصر ( لا يشكرون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address includes all who share the two prisoners' idolatry; “besides Him” means besides God.
rows.anchor: إنما جمع في الخطاب لهما لأنه أراد جميع من شاركهما في شركهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are empty names: the names have no true meanings that apply to them.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح معاني تلك الأسماء للأصنام فكأنها أسماء فارغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent no proof authorizing their worship.
rows.anchor: ( ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان ) أي من حجة بعبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God has authority to decree, command, and prohibit.
rows.anchor: أي ما القضاء والأمر والنهي إلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright religion here means affirming God's oneness.
rows.anchor: ( ذلك الدين القيم ) أي المستقيم يشير إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that most people do not know worship of anyone besides God is impermissible.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمون أنه لا يجوز عبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that most people do not know the reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمون ماللمطيعين من الثواب وللعاصين من العقاب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: A single ḍagth is a handful or bundle; plural adghāth describes a dream with disconnected parts and no interpretation.
rows.anchor: واحدها ضغث مكسورة وهي ما لا تأويل له من الرؤيا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Adghāth means confused dreams.
rows.anchor: الأضغاث الرؤيا المختلطة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The phrase means mixed-up fragments, like gathered plant bundles containing different kinds.
rows.anchor: أضغاث أحلام أي أخلاط مثل أضغاث النبات يجمعها الرجل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: A ḍagth is a bundle; the king's dream was a bundle of mixed fragments, not a clear dream.
rows.anchor: الضغث في اللغة الحزمة والباقة من الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers say they cannot interpret dreams of this confused kind.
rows.anchor: ليس للرؤيا المخلتطة عندنا تأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams are what a person sees in sleep, whether valid or false.
rows.anchor: والأحلام جمع حلم وهو ما يراه الإنسان في نومه مما يصح ومما يبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative abbreviates events: the messenger was sent, came to Joseph, and addressed him as “truthful.”
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام اختصار المعنى فأرسلوه فأتى يوسف فقال يا يوسف يا أيها الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq means one who tells much truth, on the pattern of other intensive forms.
rows.anchor: والصديق الكثير الصدق كما يقال فسيق وسكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṣiddīq had already been explained in the discussion of 4:69.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The people” means the king, his officials, and the scholars gathered to interpret the dream.
rows.anchor: يعني الملك وأصحابه والعلماء الذين جمعهم لتعبير رؤياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they would learn the interpretation of the king's dream.
rows.anchor: يعلمون تأويل رؤيا الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they would learn Joseph's standing, which might lead to his release.
rows.anchor: يعلمون بمكانك فيكون سبب خلاصك

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: One analysis connects the first “perhaps” to Joseph's interpretation and the second to the messenger's return; both mean “so that.”
rows.anchor: لعل الأولى متعلقة بالإفتاء والثانية مبنية على الرجوع وكلتاهما بمعنى كي

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the first “perhaps” mean hope and the second mean “so that”; the repetition reflects distinct senses.
rows.anchor: الأولى بمعنى عسى والثانية بمعنى كي فأعيدت لاختلاف المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same explanation accounts for the doubled “perhaps” at Joseph 12:63.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الجواب عن قوله ( لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون )

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Some say the Aziz, Joseph's former master, had died; others say he was still alive.
rows.anchor: كان سيده العزيز قد مات واشتغلت عنه امرأته وقال بعضهم لم يكن العزيز قد مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph told the cupbearer to tell the king that seven abundant years would be followed by seven harsh years unless provision was made.
rows.anchor: قل للملك هذه سبع سنين مخصبات ومن بعدهن سبع سنين شداد إلا أن يحتال لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asked the women what happened when they tried to seduce Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال ( ما خطبكن ) أي ما شأنكن وقصتكن ( إذ راودتن يوسف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for addressing all the women is that the king was identifying the individual who made the attempt.
rows.anchor: جمعهن في السؤال ليعلم عين المراودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation distinguishes the wife's attempt to seduce Joseph from the other women urging him to accept her.
rows.anchor: أزليخا راودته على نفسه وراوده باقي النسوة على القبول منها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Plural address can describe a group while meaning only one member when context removes ambiguity; the Prophet similarly addressed women collectively about Hell's majority.
rows.anchor: قد يوقع على النوع وصف الحبس إذا أمن من اللبس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says al-Ḥasan's reading with a still shīn in ḥāshā is invalid Arabic because it joins two vowelless consonants.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن بتسكين الشين ولا اختلاف بين النحويين أن الإسكان غير جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women declared Joseph innocent; the Aziz's wife then said the truth had emerged clearly.
rows.anchor: فأعلم النسوة الملك براءة يوسف من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣḥaṣ means that the truth appeared and became clear.
rows.anchor: أي برزوتبين واشتقاقه في اللغة من الحصة

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: He glosses ḥaṣḥaṣ as becoming clear and manifest.
rows.anchor: حصحص بمعنى وضح وانكشف تقول العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom about a camel settling on its knees describes it making an impression in the ground and scattering gravel.
rows.anchor: حصحص البعير في بروكة إذا تمكن وأثر في الأرض وفرق الحصى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: One view says the wife confessed because the women had exonerated Joseph and she expected them to accuse her next.
rows.anchor: لما رأت النسوة قد برأنه قالت لم يبق إلا أن يقبلن علي بالتقرير فأقرت قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another view says she confessed to show repentance and confirm Joseph's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أظهرت التوبة وحققت صدق يوسف قاله الماوردي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says dhālika, “that,” means hādhā, “this.”
rows.anchor: ذلك بمعنى هذا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Both “this” and “that” can point to a nearby event: a recent event resembles something present, yet its completion makes it seem absent.
rows.anchor: هذا وذلك يصلحان في هذا الموضع وأشباهه لقرب الخبر من أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view assigns the statement to Joseph; changes of speaker within a passage are acceptable when context makes them clear.
rows.anchor: أنه يوسف وهو من أغمض ما يأتي من الكلام أن تحكي عن شخص شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the speaker shift with examples from 7:110, 27:34–35, and 36:52, where dialogue moves between speakers without a new formula.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، ابن جريج
rows.claim: One report places Joseph's statement in prison after the cupbearer told him the women's answer to the king.
rows.anchor: لما رجع الساقي إلى يوسف فأخبره وهو في السجن بجواب امرأة العزيز والنسوة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report places Joseph's statement after he appeared before the king.
rows.anchor: أنه قاله بعد حضوره مجلس الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to Joseph's act of sending back the king's messenger.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي فعلت من ردي رسول الملك ليعلم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، الجمهور
rows.claim: The intended knower is the Aziz, and Joseph did not betray him regarding his wife while he was away.
rows.anchor: ليعلم العزيز أني لم أخنه في امرأته ( بالغيب ) أي إذا غاب عني

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The king is the one meant by “so he may know,” while the betrayal Joseph denies was against the Aziz's household.
rows.anchor: المشار إليه بقوله ليعلم الملك والمشار إليه بقوله لم أخنه العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the king both the person who should know and the person Joseph did not betray.
rows.anchor: أن المشار إليه بالشيئين الملك فالمعنى ليعلم الملك أني لم أخنه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: If the Aziz was the king's minister, Joseph means he did not betray the king regarding his minister's wife.
rows.anchor: لكون العزيز وزيره فالمعنى لم أخنه في امرأة وزيره

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: On another account, the Aziz's wife was the king's niece, so Joseph did not betray the king regarding his niece.
rows.anchor: لم أخنه في بنت أخته وكانت أزليخا بنت أخت الملك

rows.speaker: مجاهد، ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes God the intended knower; Ibn al-Anbari says this attributes knowledge to God in wording while the practical referent is people, as at 47:31.
rows.anchor: الرابع أن المشار إليه بقوله ليعلم الله فالمعنى ليعلم الله أني لم أخنه روي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph spoke before the king, using the third person rather than direct address honored the king; if absent, or referring to the absent Aziz, the wording is natural.
rows.anchor: آثر الخطاب بالياء توقيرا للملك كما يقول الرجل للوزير إن رأى الوزير أن يوقع في قصتي

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another view assigns the statement to the Aziz's wife: Joseph should know that she did not falsely accuse him while he was absent.
rows.anchor: قول امرأة العزيز فعلى هذا يتصل بما قبله والمعنى ليعلم يوسف أني لم أخنه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: A third view assigns it to the Aziz, who says he did not neglect to reward Joseph's faithfulness.
rows.anchor: قول العزيز والمعنى ليعلم يوسف أني لم أخنه بالغيب فلم أغفل عن مجازاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “God does not guide the plotting of traitors” means He does not approve adulterers' actions.
rows.anchor: لا يصوب عمل الزناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God does not guide one who betrays a trust, but exposes him in the end.
rows.anchor: لا يرشد من خان أمانته ويفضحه في عاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The identity of the speaker has the same three alternatives discussed for the preceding verse: Joseph, the Aziz's wife, or the Aziz.
rows.anchor: في القائل لهذا ثلاثة أقوال وهي التي تقدمت في الآية قبلها

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس، الأكثرون
rows.claim: On the Joseph reading, Gabriel challenged Joseph about whether he had also been free of blame when he had desired her; Joseph replied that he did not absolve himself.
rows.anchor: لما قال ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب غمزه جبريل فقال ولا حين هممت فقال وما أبرئ نفسي

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says Joseph admitted that he had desired her when he said he had not betrayed the Aziz.
rows.anchor: لما قال لم أخنه ذكر أنه قد هم بها فقال وما أبرئ نفسي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Joseph feared his words sounded self-congratulatory, so he said he did not declare himself innocent.
rows.anchor: خاف أن يكون قد زكى نفسه فقال وما أبرئ نفسي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The king with Joseph told him to recall what he had desired, prompting his answer.
rows.anchor: قال له الملك الذي معه اذكر ما هممت به فقال وما أبرئ نفسي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The Aziz's wife challenged Joseph that he had not been innocent on the day he loosened his trousers; he answered that he did not absolve himself.
rows.anchor: قالت امرأة العزيز ولا يوم حللت سراويلك فقال وما أبرئ نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Aziz's wife is speaking, she means she does not absolve herself of having tried to seduce Joseph.
rows.anchor: هذا قول امرأة العزيز فالمعنى وما أبرئ نفسي أني كنت راودته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Aziz is speaking, he means he does not absolve himself of having suspected Joseph.
rows.anchor: هو العزيز فالمعنى وما أبرئ نفسي من سوء الظن بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters differ in how they articulate the consecutive hamzas in al-sūʾ illā: some pronounce both, while others delete, soften, shift, or assimilate a hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة ويعقوب إلا رويسا بالسوء إلا بتحقيق الهمزتين

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He calls “except what my Lord has mercy on” a disconnected exception: the sense is “except that my Lord's mercy is my support.”
rows.anchor: هذا استثناء منقطع والمعنى إلا أن رحمة ربي عليها المعتمد

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The phrase can mean “except the person whom my Lord protects.”
rows.anchor: المعنى إلا من عصم ربي

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: If the wife speaks, she means one whom God helps to overcome desire or removes desire from.
rows.anchor: إلا من رحم ربي في قهره لشهوته أو في نزعها عنه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: If the Aziz speaks, he means one whom God protects from suspicion or restrains from haste.
rows.anchor: بأن يكفيه سوء الظن أو يثبته فلا يعجل

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He says the Joseph interpretation is sounder because scholars support it and its theology suits someone who knows God, unlike an idol-worshiping woman.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن هذا قول يوسف أصح لوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators say the king recognized Joseph's innocence and trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: فلما تبين الملك عذر يوسف وعلم أمانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To “make him exclusively mine” means to make Joseph uniquely close, without sharing him with anyone.
rows.anchor: أي أجعله خالصا لي لا يشركني فيه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's summons can be explained by saying he summoned Joseph to assign him duties in a different meeting from the dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: أمر الملك باحضاره ليقلده الأعمال في غير المجلس الذي استحضره فيه لتعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: The king spoke seventy languages; Joseph answered each in that language, astonishing the king, who was told Joseph was thirty years old.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يتكلم بسبعين لسانا كان كلما كلمة بلسان أجابه يوسف بذلك اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the king's request, Joseph explained the dream and advised abundant planting in the good years and storing food for the following years.
rows.anchor: أرى أن تزرع زرعا كثيرا في هذه السنين المخصبة وتجمع الطعام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Makin and amin mean that the king had empowered Joseph within his rule and entrusted him with it.
rows.anchor: قد مكنتك في ملكي وائتمنتك فيه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Makin means high-ranking, while amin means trustworthy guardian.
rows.anchor: المكين الوجيه والأمين الحافظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasures Joseph asked to manage were the king's storehouses.
rows.anchor: أي خزائن أرضك

rows.speaker: الضحاك، الزجاج
rows.claim: One view takes the storehouses to mean the treasury and its money.
rows.anchor: خزائن الأموال قاله الضحاك والزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Another view limits the storehouses to food supplies.
rows.anchor: خزائن الطعام فحسب قاله ابن السائب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Joseph asked because prophets are sent to establish justice, and he knew no one else could administer it as well.
rows.anchor: لأن الأنبياء بعثوا بالعدل فعلم أنه لا أحد أقوم بذلك منه

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ḥafīẓ means safeguarding what was entrusted to him; ʿalīm means knowing when famine would occur.
rows.anchor: حفيظ لما وليتني عليم بالمجاعة متى تكون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ḥafīẓ means guarding what he was entrusted with; ʿalīm means understanding the coming years.
rows.anchor: حفيظ لما استودعتني عليم بهذه السنين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Ḥafīẓ means skilled at accounting and ʿalīm means knowing languages, since people came from many regions.
rows.anchor: حفيظ للحساب عليم بالألسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One account says the king appointed Joseph after a year; a prophetic report says the king would have appointed him immediately had he not asked.
rows.anchor: أنه ولاه بعد سنة روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He relates a prophetic report that adding “if God wills” would have brought Joseph kingship immediately.
rows.anchor: لو أن يوسف قال إني حفيظ عليم إن شاء الله لملك من وقته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the king accepted Islam through Joseph.
rows.anchor: أسلم الملك على يد يوسف

rows.speaker: أهل السير
rows.claim: After a year in the royal household, Joseph was enthroned and given the sword; the king delegated rule, removed Qitfir, then married Joseph to Qitfir's wife, who bore Ephraim and Misha.
rows.anchor: فلما انصرمت دعاه الملك فتوجه ورداه بسيفه وأمر له بسرير من ذهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another account, transmitted by Muqatil, says the king gave Joseph rule after a year and a half.
rows.anchor: أنه ملكه بعد سنة ونصف حكاه مقاتل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: وهب، ابن السائب
rows.claim: A third view says the king handed over authority immediately.
rows.anchor: أنه سلم إليه الأمر من وقته قاله وهب وابن السائب

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: One answer is that Joseph's failure to say “if God wills” caused a delay in his appointment.
rows.anchor: ترك الاستثناء أوجب عقوبة بأن أخر تمليكه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Another answer is that Joseph kept the qualification implicit, as his brothers did when promising to bring provisions.
rows.anchor: أضمر الاستثناء كما أضمروه في قولهم ( ونمير أهلها )

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: A third answer is that Joseph described his comparative ability, which was certain and did not require a qualification.
rows.anchor: أراد أن حفظي وعلمي يزيدان على حفظ غيري وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-praise is permissible when free of arrogance and intended to secure a right, establish justice, or end injustice.
rows.anchor: لما خلا مدحه لنفسه من بغي وتكبر وكان مراده به الوصول إلى حق يقيمه وعدل

rows.speaker: محمد بن القاسم
rows.claim: He compares this to the Prophet, Ali, and Ibn Masʿud openly describing their rank or knowledge to inform learners.
rows.anchor: أنا أكرم ولد آدم على ربه وقال علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام والله ما من آية إلا وأنا أعلم

rows.speaker: أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Joseph's story shows that a person may state his merit to someone who does not know it, without violating the prohibition on self-purification.
rows.anchor: يجوز للإنسان أن يصف نفسه بالفضل عند من لا يعرفه وأنه ليس من المحظور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits the dialogue in which the king appoints Joseph; the preceding request implies that it happened.
rows.anchor: في الكلام محذوف تقديره اجعلني على خزائن الأرض قال قد فعلت فحذف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enabling Joseph in Egypt matched His earlier rescue from harm and prison and his closeness to the king.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك الإنعام الذي أنعما عليه في دفع المكروه عنه وتخليصه من السجن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Yatabawwaʾ means that Joseph settled wherever he wanted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ينزل حيث أراد

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، المفضل
rows.claim: They recited “where We will” with nūn rather than “where he will.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والمفضل حيث نشاء بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God singles out whom He wills for the blessings of prophethood and deliverance.
rows.anchor: نختص بنعمتنا من النبوة والنجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “doers of good” whose reward God does not waste are believers.
rows.anchor: ( من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين ) يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted story says Joseph sold Egypt's people food first for their wealth and property, then for their persons; he later persuaded the king to free them and return their property.
rows.anchor: يقال إن يوسف باع أهل مصر الطعام بأموالهم وحليهم ومواشيهم وعقارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story says Joseph did not eat his fill during the famine so that he would remember the hungry.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف لا يشبع في تلك الأيام ويقول إني أخاف أن أنسى الجائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's reward in the afterlife surpasses what he received in this world; the same applies to believers who follow his path of patience.
rows.anchor: ما نعطي يوسف في الآخرة خير مما أعطيناه في الدنيا وكذلك غيره من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the king entrusted Egypt to Joseph, he treated people gently, called them to Islam, and they believed in and loved him; famine then reached Canaan, so Jacob sent his sons for grain.
rows.anchor: تلطف يوسف للناس ولم يزل يدعوهم إلى الإسلام فآمنوا به وأحبوه فلما أصاب الناس القحط

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob told his sons to greet Egypt's just king and introduce themselves, hoping he would recognize them; Joseph knew them, while they did not know him.
rows.anchor: انطلقوا إليه وأقرئوه مني السلام وانتسبوا له لعله يعرفكم

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the story, Joseph suspected the brothers were spies; they explained their father's identity, their famine, and their lost brother, after which he demanded their youngest brother.
rows.anchor: جئتم تنظرون عورة بلدي فقالوا لا والله ولكنا من كنعان

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says the brothers spoke Hebrew and Joseph used an interpreter to make them think he suspected them of spying; they explained their family and left Shimon as a hostage.
rows.anchor: لما دخلوا عليه كلموه بالعبرانية فأمر الترجمان فكلمهم ليشبه عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view says Joseph recognized his brothers immediately by seeing them.
rows.anchor: أنه عرفهم برؤيتهم قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph did not recognize them until they identified themselves to him.
rows.anchor: أنه ما عرفهم حتى تعرفوا إليه قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The brothers did not recognize Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل لا يعرفونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they expected an unbelieving king and did not examine him closely enough to dispel doubt.
rows.anchor: جاؤوه مقدرين أنه ملك كافر فلم يتأملوا منه ما يزول به عنهم الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Joseph's dress and jewelry made him unrecognizable.
rows.anchor: عاينوا من زيه وحليته ما كان سببا لإنكارهم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph wore silk clothing and a gold collar.
rows.anchor: كان لا بسا ثياب حرير وفي عنقه طوق من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Joseph had exceptional beauty, they had left him as a child and saw him grown; appearances change, and they never expected him to become so powerful.
rows.anchor: فارقوه طفلا ورأوه كبيرا والأحوال تتغير وما توهموا أنه ينال هذه المرتبة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: “Half the beauty” means God set a limit for beauty and gave Joseph half of that maximum, making him nearly as beautiful as the finest beings; it does not mean everyone else received the other half.
rows.anchor: أن الله جعل للحسن غاية وحدا وجعله لمن شاء من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahhaztu means preparing what people need; household equipment means its belongings.
rows.anchor: يقال جهزت القوم تجهيزا إذا هيأت لهم ما يصلحهم وجهاز البيت متاعه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Joseph loaded one camel for each brother.
rows.anchor: حمل لكل رجل منهم بعيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I give full measure” means completing the measure without shortchanging them.
rows.anchor: أي أتمه ولا أبخسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Best of hosts” means the best providers of hospitality, as Joseph treated them generously.
rows.anchor: يعني المضيفين وذلك أنه أحسن ضيافتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph threatens that without their brother they will receive no measure from him.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters understand the threat to apply to future visits.
rows.anchor: أنه يعني به فيما بعد وهو قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph withheld their measure on that very occasion.
rows.anchor: أنه منعهم الكيل في الحال قاله وهب بن منبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to seek their father's agreement; murāwadah means strenuous pursuit of a request.
rows.anchor: أي نطلبه منه والمراودة الاجتهاد في الطلب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: “We will do it” means they would bring Benjamin and guarantee his arrival.
rows.anchor: وإنا لجاؤوك به وضامنون لك المجيء به هذا مذهب الكلبي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another reading takes “we will do it” as emphasis on their promise to persuade their father.
rows.anchor: أنه توكيد قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: A third reading means they would keep pressing their father and continue counseling him to send Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وإنما لمديمون المطالبة به لأبينا ومتابعون المشورة عليه بتوجيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of five explanations for Joseph's request, the sound one is that God commanded it as a further trial for Jacob, increasing his reward.
rows.anchor: زيادة لبلاء يعقوب ليعظم ثوابه وهذا الأظهر

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Joseph did not originally intend to detain Benjamin; after Benjamin recognized him and asked to stay, Joseph said he needed to accuse him of a grave matter to keep him.
rows.anchor: طلبه لا ليحبسه فلما عرفه قال لا أفارقك يا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed purpose was to prompt Jacob to realize Joseph's situation.
rows.anchor: أن يكون قصد تنبيه يعقوب بذلك على حال يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed purpose was to multiply Jacob's joy when both sons returned.
rows.anchor: ليتضاعف سرور يعقوب برجوع ولديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed purpose was to bring Benjamin the joy of reunion before the other brothers.
rows.anchor: ليعجل سرور أخيه باجتماعه به قبل إخوته

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: In a report, Jacob later asked Joseph why he had not sent word; Joseph said Gabriel had ordered him not to, and Gabriel said God had ordered it because Jacob had feared the wolf but not trusted God.
rows.anchor: قل ليعقوب خفت عليه الذئب ولم تؤمني

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read “to his young men” with the collective fityah form.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم لفتيته

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read “to his young men” as fityān.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم لفتيانه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Fityah is a small-count plural and fityān a large-count plural; both refer to servants here.
rows.anchor: الفتية جمع فتى في العدد القليل والفتيان في الكثير والمعنى قال لغلمانه

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph returned their money because he feared Jacob might lack enough currency for another trip.
rows.anchor: تخوف أن لا يكون عند أبيه من الورق ما يرجعون به مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He wanted them to recognize the money and feel unable to keep it without returning it.
rows.anchor: أراد أنهم إذا عرفوها لم يستحلوا إمساكها حتى يردوها

rows.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري، أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: He disliked taking payment from his needy father and brothers, so he secretly returned it as generosity.
rows.anchor: استقبح أخذ الثمن من والده وإخوته مع حاجتهم إليه فرده عليهم من حيث لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: He wanted them to know he was not asking them back out of greed for their money.
rows.anchor: ليعلموا أن طلبه لعودهم لم يكن طمعا في أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph displayed generosity and kindness to make their return more likely.
rows.anchor: أراهم كرمه وبره ليكون أدعى إلى عودهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The brothers praised their host to Jacob, saying no descendant of Jacob had treated them as generously.
rows.anchor: قدمنا على خير رجل أنزلنا وأكرمنا كرامة لو كان رجلا من ولد يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph had already withheld their measure, “we were denied measure” plainly describes what happened.
rows.anchor: فإن قلنا إنه لم يكل لهم فلفظ منع بين

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: If Joseph only threatened to withhold their future measure, the brothers speak as though the future denial had already been decreed.
rows.anchor: حكم علينا بمنع الكيل بعد هذا الوقت كما تقول للرجل دخلت والله النار

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Alternatively, “we were denied” abbreviates “he will deny us” if Jacob does not send Benjamin, as in other Qurʾanic past-for-future expressions.
rows.anchor: يا أبانا يمنع منا الكيل إن لم ترسله معنا فناب منع عن يمنع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، عاصم، ابن عامر
rows.claim: They recited naktal with nūn: “we will obtain measure.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر نكتل بالنون

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
rows.claim: They recited yaktal with yāʾ; the sense remains that they will obtain measure if Benjamin comes.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي يكتل بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob will not trust them with Benjamin any more than he trusted them with Joseph, since that trust failed.
rows.anchor: لا آمنكم إلا كأمني على يوسف يريد أنه لم ينفعه ذلك الأمن إذ خانوه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read khayrun ḥifẓan, “better in preserving.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وابو بكر عن عاصم حفظا

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read khayrun ḥāfiẓan, “a better guardian.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم خير حافظا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On the ḥāfiẓan reading, the accusative is a specification (tamyīz), not a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ونصبه على التمييز دون الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “provisions” are the containers that held the food.
rows.anchor: يعني أوعية الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The returned goods were the money they had carried as payment for the food.
rows.anchor: أوعية الطعام ( وجدوا بضاعتهم ) التي حملوها ثمنا للطعام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ruddat derives from rudadtu with two dāls assimilated; a kasra reading transfers the vowel from the first dāl, as in qīla and bīʿa.
rows.anchor: الأصل رددت فأدغمت الدال الأولى في الثانية وبقيت الراء مضمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes mā nabghī as a question: “What more could we want, when our goods have been returned?”
rows.anchor: أنها استفهام المعنى أي شيء نبغي وقد ردت بضاعتنا إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes it a negation: they need no money from Jacob because the returned payment will fund their return; they hope to reassure him.
rows.anchor: أنها نافية المعنى ما نبغي شيئا أي لسنا نطلب منك دراهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن يعمر، الجحدري، أبو حيوة
rows.claim: They read tabghī with tāʾ, addressing Jacob.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن يعمر والجحدري وأبو حيوة ما تبغي بالتاء على الخطاب ليعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namīr means bringing food to one's family.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ( ونمير أهلنا ) أي نجلب لهم الطعام

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He defines māra as carrying provisions from outside one's home region to one's family.
rows.anchor: مار أهله يميرهم ميرا وهو مائر لأهله إذا حمل إليهم أقواتهم من غير بلده

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: “We will guard our brother” means the Benjamin they are asking Jacob to send.
rows.anchor: نحفظ أخانا بنيامين الذي ترسله معنا قاله الأكثرون

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view identifies the brother as Shimon, whom Joseph held as a hostage.
rows.anchor: ونحفظ أخانا شمعون الذي أخذه رهينة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expect one additional camel-load for their brother because Joseph limited each person to one camel-load.
rows.anchor: يعنون بذلك نصيب أخيهم لأن يوسف كان لا يعطي الواحد أكثر من حمل بعير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: “That is an easy measure” means the king quickly grants their measure when Benjamin comes.
rows.anchor: ذلك كيل سريع لا حبس فيه يعنون إذا جاء معنا عجل الملك لنا الكيل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: It can mean that the requested measure is easy for the ruler to grant.
rows.anchor: ذلك كيل سهل على الذي نمضي إليه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: It can instead mean the measure they brought is small and insufficient for them.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي جئناك به كيل يسير لا يقنعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob required a reliable covenant, meaning an oath by God that they would bring Benjamin back.
rows.anchor: أي تعطوني عهدا أثق به والمعنى حتى تحلفوا لي بالله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The lām in “you will surely bring him” answers an implied oath: “and you say, by God, we will bring him.”
rows.anchor: وهذه اللام جواب لمضمر تلخيصه وتقولوا والله لتأتنني به

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The exception “unless you are surrounded” means that all of them are killed.
rows.anchor: أن يهلك جميعكم قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: It can mean that they become unable to bring Benjamin because something blocks them.
rows.anchor: أن يحال بينكم وبينه فلا تقدرون على الإتيان به

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One account says they swore by the rank of Muhammad with his Lord.
rows.anchor: حلفوا له بحق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ومنزلته من ربه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Another account says they swore by God.
rows.anchor: حلفوا بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “God is a trustee over what we say” means God is witness.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه الشهيد والثاني كفيل بالوفاء رويا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God guarantees fulfillment of the pledge.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه الشهيد والثاني كفيل بالوفاء رويا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: As the family prepared to travel, Jacob told his sons not to enter Egypt together through one entrance.
rows.anchor: لما تجهزوا للرحيل قال لهم يعقوب لا تدخلوا يعني مصر من باب واحد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The entrance means one of Egypt's city gates; Egypt was said to have four gates.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد بابا من أبواب مصر وكان لمصر أربعة أبواب

rows.speaker: السدي، أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view takes the entrances to mean the roads into Egypt, not its gates.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد الطرق لا الأبواب قاله السدي وروى نحوه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: Jacob feared the evil eye because his sons were handsome and strong.
rows.anchor: أنه خاف عليهم العين وكانوا أولي جمال وقوة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Jacob feared they might be assassinated because they were suspected in Egypt.
rows.anchor: أنه خاف أن يغتالوا لماظهر لهم في أرض مصر من التهمة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Jacob wanted the brothers to meet Joseph in private.
rows.anchor: أنه أحب أن يلقوا يوسف في خلوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob could not avert God's decree; the next verse confirms that his precaution could not protect them from what God decreed.
rows.anchor: لن أدفع عنكم شيئا قضاه الله فإنه إن شاء أهلككم متفرقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's instruction reflected his concern for his sons, not power over God's decree.
rows.anchor: وهي إرادته أن يكون دخولهم كذلك شفقة عليهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The exception about Jacob's desire is disconnected: the sense is “but there was a need in Jacob's heart which he fulfilled.”
rows.anchor: إلا حاجة استثناء ليس من الأول والمعنى لكن حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qadāhā means Jacob made his wish known and spoke of it.
rows.anchor: قضاها أي أبداها وتكلم بها

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob was knowledgeable in preserving the instruction God had taught him.
rows.anchor: إنه حافظ لما علمناه

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob knew that entering through separate gates could not avert God's decree.
rows.anchor: وإنه لذو علم أن دخلوهم من أبواب متفرقة لا يغني عنهم من الله شيئا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Jacob acted on the knowledge God had given him; action is called knowledge because knowledge begins action.
rows.anchor: وإنه لعامل بما علم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Jacob was certain of God's promise.
rows.anchor: وإنه لمتيقن لوعدنا

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Jacob kept God's instruction.
rows.anchor: وإنه لحافظ لوصيتنا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Jacob knew that only what God decreed could befall his sons.
rows.anchor: وإنه لعالم بما علمناه أنه لا يصيب بنيه إلا ما قضاه الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Jacob had knowledge through God's teaching him.
rows.anchor: وإنه لذو علم لتعليمنا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brother is Benjamin, Joseph's full brother through both parents, and Joseph brought him close.
rows.anchor: يعني بنيامين وكان أخاه لأبيه وأمه قاله قتادة وضمه إليه وأنزله معه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Benjamin was Joseph's brother by both father and mother.
rows.anchor: وكان أخاه لأبيه وأمه قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Āwaytu with long alif means I brought someone to myself; aw aytu with short alif means I sought refuge among people.
rows.anchor: آويت فلانا إلي بمد الألف إذا ضممته إليك وأويت إلى بني فلان بقصر الألف

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: One view says Joseph openly told Benjamin he was his brother after asking his name and their mother's name.
rows.anchor: فقال إني أنا أخوك قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وكذلك قال ابن إسحاق أخبره أنه يوسف

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph initially said he would be Benjamin's replacement brother, then revealed himself after their conversation and reunion.
rows.anchor: لم يعترف له بذلك وإنما قال أنا أخوك مكان أخيك الهالك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Fala tabtaʾis means do not grieve or be sad.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة لا تأس ولا تحزن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Fala tabtaʾis means do not grieve or become subdued.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج لا تحزن ولا تستكن

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Tabtaʾis derives from buʾs, hardship and distress; Joseph tells Benjamin not to suffer distress over their brothers' actions.
rows.anchor: تبتئس تفتعل من البؤس وهو الضر والشدة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph may mean the brothers' mockery of him and Benjamin for their maternal grandfather's idol worship.
rows.anchor: كانوا يعيرون يوسف وأخاه بعبادة جدهما أبي أمهما للأصنام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Another view reads the phrase as future: Benjamin should not grieve about what the brothers will do when they accuse him of stealing; kānū can mean “will be.”
rows.anchor: لا تحزن بما سيعملون بعد هذا الوقت حين يسرقونك فتكون كانوا بمعنى يكونون

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poetry uses kāna of what will happen later, supporting the future reading.
rows.anchor: فلقد يكون أخا دم وذبائح

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Joseph may mean the brothers' past envy and efforts to turn their father away from him and Benjamin.
rows.anchor: لا تحزن بما عملوا من حسدنا وحرصوا على صرف وجه أبينا عنا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Joseph completed their measures, gave Benjamin his own camel-load, and put the king's cup in his baggage.
rows.anchor: أوفى لهم الكيل وحمل ل بنيامين بعيرا باسمه كما حمل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiwāʿ and siqāyah name one object, like two names for wheat or a dining tray.
rows.anchor: فهما اسمان واقعان على شيء واحد كالبر والحنطة والمائدة والخوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say ṣiwāʿ is the object's proper name while siqāyah is a descriptive term, like cup and vessel.
rows.anchor: الاسم الحقيقي الصواع والسقاية وصف كما يقال كوز وإناء

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Joseph made the cup the measuring vessel so that nobody would measure with anything else; another view says he used it to honor his brothers.
rows.anchor: جعل يوسف ذلك الصاع مكيالا لئلا يكال بغيره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: A caller is someone who announces; the form can mean announcing repeatedly or thoroughly.
rows.anchor: أعلم معلم يقال آذنته بالشيء فهو مؤذن به أي أعلمته

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: ʿAyr refers to the owners or people traveling with camels.
rows.anchor: لا يقال عير إلا لأصحاب الإبل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: ʿAyr means camels equipped for riding and loaded for travel.
rows.anchor: العير الإبل المرحولة المركوبة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: ʿAyr means the people riding camels.
rows.anchor: العير القوم على الإبل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: One answer to the accusation is that the brothers had stolen Joseph from his father by casting him into the well.
rows.anchor: إنكم لسارقون يوسف حين قطعتموه عن أبيه وطرحتموه في الجب

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Another answer says the caller did not know Joseph had ordered the cup placed in Benjamin's baggage, so the caller did not knowingly lie.
rows.anchor: أن المنادي نادى وهو لا يعلم أن يوسف أمر بوضع السقاية في رحل أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer says the caller accused them without Joseph's order.
rows.anchor: أن المنادي نادى بالتسريق لهم بغير أمر يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth takes the accusation as what it looked like to an uninformed observer, like the taunt in 44:49 or the report that Abraham spoke three apparent falsehoods.
rows.anchor: إنكم لسارقون فيما يظهر لمن لم يعلم حقيقة أخباركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the brothers turned toward the caller and his companions.
rows.anchor: على المؤذن وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the caller and his companions turned toward the brothers to accuse them.
rows.anchor: أقبل المنادي ومن معه على إخوة يوسف بالدعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mādhā tafqidūn means “What have you lost?”
rows.anchor: مالذي ضل عنكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ṣiwāʿ is the same as ṣāʿ; both words can be masculine or feminine, and the recited variants all share a basic meaning.
rows.anchor: الصواع هو الصاع بعينه وهو يذكر ويؤنث وكذلك الصاع يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ṣawgh with ghayn is a verbal noun describing a vessel cast from gold.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الصوغ بالغين المعجمة مصدر صغت وصف الإناء به لأنه كان مصوغا من ذهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Two reports identify the cup as either beryl or copper.
rows.anchor: أنه كان قدحا من زبرجد والثاني أنه كان من نحاس رويا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says it was a silver drinking cup ornamented with jewels.
rows.anchor: كان شربة من فضة مرصعة بالجوهر قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He says it was a gold goblet.
rows.anchor: كان كأسا من ذهب قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He transmits another view that the cup was made of copper alloy.
rows.anchor: كان من مس حكاه الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One description says the vessel was long and resembled a small grain measure.
rows.anchor: أنه كان مستطيلا يشبه المكوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another description says it resembled a shallow basin.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يشبه الطاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announced reward was a camel's load of food, and the caller guaranteed it to whoever returned the cup.
rows.anchor: يعني الصواع ( حمل بعير ) من الطعام ( وأنا به زعيم ) أي كفيل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Tāllāh means wallāh, but the oath-letter tāʾ is used only with God's name, not al-Raḥmān or “my Lord.”
rows.anchor: تالله بمعنى والله إلا أن التاء لا يقسم بها إلى في الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The tāʾ in the oath derives from wāw, as in other Arabic forms where tāʾ replaces initial wāw.
rows.anchor: أبدلت التاء من الواو كما أبدلت في التخمة والتراث والتجاه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The oath form developed with God's name because swearing by Allah is common, whereas swearing by al-Raḥmān was not commonly used.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستعمال في الإقسام كثر بالله ولم يكن بالرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers addressed Joseph when saying “you know.”
rows.anchor: يعنون يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial means they had not come to wrong anyone or steal.
rows.anchor: أي لنظلم أحدا أو نسرق

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس، مقاتل
rows.claim: They said Egyptians knew their honesty because they had returned their money, which exceeded the cup's value.
rows.anchor: لأنهم رددوا الدراهم ولا يستحلوها فالمعنى لقد علمتم أنا رددنا عليكم دراهمكم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers had muzzled their camels and donkeys so the animals would not take anything; Egyptians knew others did not do this.
rows.anchor: لما دخلوا مصر كعموا أفواه إبلهم وحميرهم حتى لا تتناول شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer is that Egyptians already knew the brothers did not wrong people.
rows.anchor: أهل مصر كانوا قد عرفوهم أنهم لا يظلمون أحدا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: In “what is its recompense,” the pronoun may refer either to the thief or to the theft.
rows.anchor: إن شئت رددت الكناية إلى السارق وإن شئت رددتها إلى السرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you are lying” refers to their statement that they were not thieves.
rows.anchor: أي في قولكم ( وما كنا سارقين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers said the person found with the cup should be enslaved as his punishment.
rows.anchor: أي يستعبد بذلك قال ابن عباس وهذه كانت سنة آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Enslavement was the practice of Jacob's family.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وهذه كانت سنة آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The caller brought them back to Joseph for a search; Joseph searched their bags first to dispel suspicion, then found the cup in Benjamin's bag.
rows.anchor: لإزالة التهمة فلما وصل إلى وعاء أخيه قال ما أظن هذا أخذ شيئا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The brothers protested that Benjamin had been framed with the cup, just as Joseph had placed their returned money in their bags; Joseph had already told Benjamin the plan.
rows.anchor: فقال وضع هذا في رحلي الذي وضع الدراهم في رحالكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in “then he extracted it” refers to the theft.
rows.anchor: أنها ترجع إلى السرقة قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the siqāyah, the vessel.
rows.anchor: والثاني إلى السقاية قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to ṣiwāʿ, on the reading that treats it as feminine.
rows.anchor: إلى الصواع على لغة من أنثه

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: “We schemed for Joseph” means “we did this for him.”
rows.anchor: كذلك صنعنا له قاله الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The phrase means “we contrived for him”; kayd means a stratagem.
rows.anchor: احتلنا له والكيد الحيلة قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: He glosses the phrase as “we intended for Joseph.”
rows.anchor: أردنا ليوسف ذكره ابن القاسم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: God's concealed arrangement raised Joseph's rank and completed His blessing, resembling human plotting because plotters hide their plans.
rows.anchor: لما دبر الله ليوسف ما دبر من ارتفاع المنزلة وكمال النعمة

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Dīn al-malik means the king's rule or political authority.
rows.anchor: أنه السلطان فالمعنى في سلطان الملك

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Dīn al-malik means the king's judicial law: theft brought beating and a fine, not imprisonment.
rows.anchor: أنه القضاء فالمعنى في قضاء الملك لأن قضاء الملك أن من سرق إنما يضرب ويغرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired the brothers to declare enslavement the thief's penalty, enabling Joseph to keep Benjamin.
rows.anchor: فأجرى الله على ألسنة إخوته أن جزاء السارق الاسترقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “unless God wills” is that God willed Joseph to attain his aim and detain Benjamin.
rows.anchor: تى أظفره بمراده بمشيئة الله فذلك معنى قوله ( إلا أن يشاء الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God would reveal a cause by which Benjamin deserved to be kept.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يشاء الله إظهار علة يستحق بها أخاه

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb recited the verbs in “We raise the degrees of whom We will” in the third person, with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب يرفع درجات من يشاء بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read darajāt with nunation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة درجات بالتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises people by varied gifts, honors, knowledge, mastery of desire, and guidance, as He raised Joseph.
rows.anchor: نرفع الدرجات بصنوف العطاء وأنواع الكرامات وابواب العلوم وقهر الهوى والتوفيق للهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Above every learned person whom God raises is someone more learned, until knowledge culminates in God; no one else has perfect knowledge.
rows.anchor: حتى ينتهي العلم إلى الله تعالى والكمال في العلم معدوم من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Joseph knew more than his brothers, while someone above Joseph knew more still.
rows.anchor: يوسف أعلم من إخوته وفوقه من هو أعلم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation emphasizes that knowledge is too vast to be comprehended completely.
rows.anchor: نبه على تعظيم العلم وبين أنه أكثر من أن يحاط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation teaches scholars humility so they do not become conceited.
rows.anchor: تعليم للعالم التواضع لئلا يعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say Benjamin stole and claim that Joseph had stolen before him.
rows.anchor: يعنون بنيامين ( فقد سرق أخ له من قبل ) يعنون يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say Joseph was punished three times: he asked the cupbearer to remember him, said he had not betrayed the Aziz, and accused his brothers of stealing.
rows.anchor: عوقب يوسف ثلاث مرات قال للساقي اذكرني عند ربك

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One alleged earlier theft was food Joseph took from his father's table during famine to give to the poor.
rows.anchor: كان يسرق الطعام من مائدة أبيه في سني المجاعة فيطعمه للمساكين

rows.speaker: أبو مالك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report says Joseph stole a kohl container from his aunt.
rows.anchor: أنه سرق مكحلة لخالته

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، وهب بن منبه، قتادة
rows.claim: They say Joseph stole his maternal grandfather's idol, broke it, and threw it into the road.
rows.anchor: سرق صنما لجده أبي أمه فكسره وألقاه في الطريق

rows.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
rows.claim: Joseph's aunt, Isaac's eldest child, tied Isaac's belt under Joseph's clothes so she could keep him when Jacob asked for him; the brothers later reproached him for it.
rows.anchor: فعمدت إلى منطقة إسحاق فربطتها على يوسف تحت ثيابه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One account says the object Joseph gave a beggar was an egg.
rows.anchor: أنه كان بيضة قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Another account says the object was a sheep.
rows.anchor: أنه شاة قاله كعب

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Another account says the object was a chicken.
rows.anchor: والثالث دجاجة قاله سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي، إدريس الأودي
rows.claim: They say Joseph hid a piece of meat from the meal, which his brothers reproached as theft.
rows.anchor: نظر يوسف إلى عرق فخبأه فعيروه بذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: None of these acts legally constitutes theft; the brothers likened them to theft in anger.
rows.anchor: ليس في هذه الأفعال كلها ما يوجب السرقة لكنها تشبه السرقة فعيره إخوته بذلك عند الغضب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The brothers were lying about Joseph having stolen anything.
rows.anchor: أنهم كذبوا عليه فيما نسبوه إليه قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو رزين، ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: They recited “he stole” with ḍamma on sīn, kasra on rāʾ, and a doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين وابن أبي عبلة فقد سرق بضم السين وكسر الراء وتشديدها

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The pronoun in “Joseph concealed it” refers to the words he says next: “You are worse in position.”
rows.anchor: أنها ترجع إلى الكلمة التي ذكرت بعد هذا وهي قوله ( أنتم شر مكانا ) روى هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the brothers' accusation that Joseph's brother had stolen; Joseph kept his answer to that accusation inside.
rows.anchor: ترجع إلى الكلمة التي قالوها في حقه وهي قولهم فقد سرق أخ له من قبل

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the argument Joseph concealed in response to their claim of theft.
rows.anchor: ترجع إلى الحجة المعنى فأسر الاحتجاج عليهم في ادعائهم عليه السرقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “You are worse in position” means the brothers' conduct was worse than Joseph's because they wronged their brother and disobeyed their father.
rows.anchor: شر صنيعا من يوسف لما قدمتم عليه من ظلم أخيكم وعقوق أبيكم

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the brothers held a worse standing with God.
rows.anchor: شر منزلة عند الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Describing what the brothers said as “what you describe” means what you say.
rows.anchor: أحدهما تقولون قاله مجاهد والثاني بما تكذبون قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another explanation is “what you lie about.”
rows.anchor: أحدهما تقولون قاله مجاهد والثاني بما تكذبون قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The sense is that God knows whether Joseph's brother really stole.
rows.anchor: المعنى والله أعلم أسرق أخ له أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted tale says Joseph made the cup speak: it recited the brothers' history, Benjamin challenged it about Joseph, and the cup answered that Joseph was alive; it then defended being asked who placed it in Benjamin's bag.
rows.anchor: نقر الصواع ثم أدناه من أذنه فقال إن صواعي هذا يخبرني أنكم كنتم اثنى عشر رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to free Benjamin, the brothers ask Joseph to take a substitute because their father is an elderly man.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يجدوا إلى خلاص أخيهم سبيلا سألوه أن يأخذ منهم بديلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A great elder” can describe Jacob's advanced age in years or his stature and importance.
rows.anchor: أي في سنة وقيل في قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We see you as a doer of good” may refer to Joseph's past conduct.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما فيما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively they appeal to Joseph's future kindness, asking him to show it now.
rows.anchor: والثاني إن فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seeks refuge in God from taking an innocent person in place of the guilty person.
rows.anchor: قد سبق تفسيره [ يوسف 33 ] والمعنى أعوذ بالله أن نأخذ بريئا بسقيم
